chunks: From him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer and fasting in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), so he said: 'Complete them, even if it is a single prayer.'

key_terms.إِتْمَامِ: Completing (prayer/fasting) as opposed to shortening or breaking
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries (referring to Mecca and Medina)

ai.seo_question: Do travelers shorten their prayer and fast in Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the ruling of travelers in the two holy sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), establishing that they must perform full (complete) prayer and fast, rather than shortening or breaking their obligations. The phrase 'even if for a single prayer' underscores that the status of a traveler persists regardless of the brevity of their stay within these sacred boundaries. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the sanctuaries from other places where a traveler might be considered a resident after a certain period.
